question:
A 42-year-old male undergoing carboplatin and etoposide chemotherapy for extensive-stage small-cell
lung cancer presents to the emergency department with a temperature of 38.5°C and mild fatigue
during a scheduled midcycle toxicity assessment. His medical history includes well-controlled
hypertension. On examination, his vital signs show a heart rate of 72/min, respiratory rate of 13/min,
and blood pressure of 107/69 mm Hg. His chest examination is unremarkable, and his abdomen is
non-tender. His implanted port shows no signs of infection at the insertion site. Laboratory results
reveal an absolute neutrophil count of 100 cells/mm³ (normal range: 1900-7600), down from normal
levels one week ago. Liver and kidney function tests are within normal limits. Chest imaging shows an

unchanged central mass without evidence of pneumonia. Urinalysis is normal, with blood and urine
cultures pending. What is the most appropriate next step in management? Answer Choices: (A) Admit
for observation and initiate broad-spectrum antipseudomonal coverage with high-dose intravenous
piperacillin-tazobactam (B) After a brief period of observation, discharge with oral ciprofloxacin and
amoxicillin-clavulanate, and follow up the next day (C) Discharge with oral doxycycline and schedule a
follow-up in 24 hours (D) Initiate granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) therapy and discharge
with no antibiotics (E) Perform a bone marrow biopsy to evaluate for unexpected myelosuppression
before initiating treatment (F) Admit for observation and initiate empiric broad-spectrum therapy with
intravenous (IV) vancomycin, high-dose IV cefepime, and IV fluconazole (G) Admit for observation and
initiate broad-spectrum antipseudomonal coverage with IV meropenem and vancomycin (H) Start oral
azithromycin and monitor closely as an outpatient (I) Admit for observation and initiate empiric
antifungal therapy with IV amphotericin B (J) Discharge with oral levofloxacin and schedule a follow-up
in 48 hours
 A. Discharge with oral levofloxacin and schedule a follow-up in 48 hours
B. Discharge with oral doxycycline and schedule a follow-up in 24 hours
C. Admit for observation and initiate empiric antifungal therapy with IV amphotericin B
D. Perform a bone marrow biopsy to evaluate for unexpected myelosuppression before initiating
treatment
E. Admit for observation and initiate empiric broad-spectrum therapy with intravenous (IV)
vancomycin, high-dose IV cefepime, and IV fluconazole
F. Start oral azithromycin and monitor closely as an outpatient
G. After a brief period of observation, discharge with oral ciprofloxacin and amoxicillin-clavulanate,
and follow up the next day
H. Admit for observation and initiate broad-spectrum antipseudomonal coverage with high-dose
intravenous piperacillin-tazobactam
I. Admit for observation and initiate broad-spectrum antipseudomonal coverage with IV meropenem
and vancomycin
J. Initiate granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) therapy and discharge with no antibiotics
